items.title: Employers Still Want MBAs – But 1 In 3 Are Replacing Entry-Level Roles With AI, GMAC Finds
items.summary: The Graduate Management Admission Council's (GMAC) 2026 Corporate Recruiters Survey reveals that while overall confidence in business graduate hiring remains high, one in three employers has already replaced some entry-level roles with AI tools, making "AI fluency" an absolute baseline expectation.

items.title: New grads have to compete with AI for entry
items.summary: Highlighting a tightening entry-level market, a report from ResumeTemplates.com shows that 48% of hiring managers would rather invest in AI tools than hire and train a recent college graduate, placing greater pressure on business majors to walk in with proven technological and workflow competencies.

items.title: The skills employers actually want in 2026
items.source: University of Florida (UFL) Warrington College of Business
items.summary: To combat the shift in entry-level hiring, top business schools are integrating a "use-manage-develop" AI framework directly into undergraduate and master's curriculums, preparing business graduates to capture the 56% wage premium commanded by workers who can effectively manage and lead AI initiatives.

items.title: Data Science & AI Initiative
items.summary: As generative AI automates routine data analysis and technical outputs, business school experts suggest that the value of business education is rapidly pivoting toward building leaders with strong strategic judgment and complex problem-solving abilities that machines cannot easily replicate.

items.title: 2026 Why Healthcare Professionals Are Moving Into AI
items.summary: Driven by a projected 30% job growth in medical AI roles through 2028, healthcare professionals are increasingly transitioning into specialized tech-driven careers—such as clinical AI product managers and workflow consultants—to optimize administrative processes and manage complex AI outputs.

items.title: PwC's 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer
items.summary: The report highlights a "two-track" labor market where AI "professionalizes" expert roles (such as radiologists and clinicians) by automating repetitive tasks, resulting in twice the job growth and higher salary premiums for roles that demand uniquely human skills like clinical judgment, leadership, and empathy.

items.title: Healthcare AI Hiring Trends 2026
items.summary: Recruitment data shows that US hospital systems are aggressively expanding their AI-specific personnel, doubling headcounts to support the rapid rollout of ambient digital scribes, governance protocols, and clinical platform management.

items.title: How AI Will Reshape the Workforce
items.summary: Healthcare executives emphasize that while AI is taking over cognitive and administrative work like scheduling and discharge planning, new graduates and clinicians must focus heavily on human-centric skills, including ethical oversight and clinical empathy.

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of Art Studies Degree Careers
items.summary: This comprehensive report details how AI is reshaping art careers, finding that while automation is reducing entry-level tasks like asset formatting and routine image editing, it is simultaneously boosting demand for interdisciplinary roles like AI-assisted art curators and digital media producers.

items.title: AI Isn’t Replacing Creativity. It’s Moving It Upstream.
items.summary: Industry leaders at Brooklyn's Artist and the Machine summit discussed how AI's automation of the technical production layer is shifting the premium value of creative work back toward human authorship, curation, design intent, and emotional intelligence.

items.title: The Best Paid Emerging Creative Roles in 2026: From Creative Technologist to AI Product Manager
items.summary: The piece highlights how traditional creative roles are morphing from simple execution into strategic, tech-integrated paths, leading to the rise of specialized hybrid titles like AI Creative Operations Lead, Synthetic Media Producer, and Conversational UX Writer.

items.title: AI Is Changing Creative Work, but the Arts Aren't Disappearing
items.summary: A study of the US creative workforce reveals that although artists frequently use AI to accelerate early-stage ideation and manage administrative tasks, there is little evidence that the technology has broadly reduced overall earnings for artists, suggesting adaptation over displacement.

items.title: Revenge of the Communicators: HR Teams Are Suddenly Scrambling for Good Liberal Arts Talent
items.summary: This trend analysis highlights how Southern California organizations are increasingly targeting arts and liberal arts graduates for communication-centric roles, valuing their storytelling, critical thinking, and audience-awareness skills as technical outputs become commoditized by AI.

items.title: A Tech Founder Called Me 'Uniquely Unqualified.' 40 Years Later, I'm Convinced My Liberal Arts Background Is the Ultimate AI Defense.
items.summary: Harvard Business School Senior Lecturer Lou Shipley explains that a liberal arts education teaches students how to learn rapidly and remain deeply curious, which ultimately builds far greater long-term career resilience as AI continues to automate hard technical skills.

items.title: Why the liberal arts can help young Americans prepare for the era of AI
items.summary: Career and educational experts note that as generative AI automates routine mathematical and coding tasks, employer demand is shifting toward workers with high emotional intelligence (EQ), critical thinking, and the lateral thinking skills nurtured by the humanities.

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of Humanities Degree Careers
items.summary: This comprehensive career analysis highlights a 30% growth in ethical AI development and digital storytelling roles over the last five years, noting that humanities graduates who upskill with basic data and digital literacy are commanding premium salaries.

items.title: Why AI is ‘resurrecting’ the liberal arts for the Class of 2026
items.summary: Vice President for Innovation and Career Development Andy Chan argues that AI has effectively commodified the "how" of technical execution, placing a substantial premium on the "liberal arts brain" to supply the critical thinking and ethical oversight required to define the "what" and the "why" of corporate projects.

items.title: College Majors With The Best Job Prospects In 2026
items.summary: According to a LinkedIn labor market study, social science graduates are in a resilient "sweet spot" because their versatile, human-centric skills like relationship-building and qualitative communication are highly valued in the AI era and easily transfer across diverse, non-traditional industries.

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of Sociology Degree Careers
items.summary: This report highlights how AI is automating routine data entry tasks in the social sciences, leading to a projected 15% growth in high-demand "hybrid" roles like Social Data Scientists who merge sociological principles with machine learning to interpret human behavior.

items.title: AI and the Labor Market: Revolution or Evolution?
items.summary: Referencing a Lumina Gallup report, this analysis reveals that social science and humanities students are among the least likely to change majors due to AI fears, as their coursework emphasizes the ethical reasoning, cultural context, and human judgment that AI cannot replicate.

items.title: Implications for Research Training and Careers
items.summary: Highlighting takeaways from the 2026 AI in Social Science Conference at the University of Chicago, this article notes that social science graduate programs are rapidly integrating computational methods and AI ethics to meet a job market that heavily favors hybrid researchers who can combine AI tools with qualitative methodologies.

items.title: DeepMind's CEO says STEM students can use AI 10 times more effectively
items.summary: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis argued that rather than making technical degrees redundant, AI tools will be utilized up to ten times more effectively by STEM and computer science graduates who possess a deep, fundamental understanding of software architecture and engineering principles.

items.title: AI Impact on Student Career Choices: Survey Reveals 4 in 10 Rethinking College Majors
items.summary: Driven by AI's workforce integration, college enrollment patterns are shifting, with general computer science programs experiencing declines while multidisciplinary engineering fields (such as mechanical, electrical, and biomedical) see gains due to their blending of physical hardware with software.

items.title: PwC’s 2026 AI Jobs Barometer
items.summary: The global analysis highlights that the average wage premium for job candidates with AI skills has surged to 62% in 2026, while emphasizing that employers are heavily prioritizing technical candidates who can combine AI capability with human-centric skills like judgment and leadership.

items.title: Top STEM Jobs for AI Career Advancement
items.summary: With over 88% of organizations now utilizing AI in their operations, a significant skills gap has emerged, presenting STEM graduates with rapid hiring spikes and lucrative career paths in machine learning engineering, data science, and AI workflow optimization.

items.title: AI is everyone's job now
items.summary: New data from Indeed reveals that "AI-touched" job titles have more than tripled since 2022 and are rapidly spreading beyond tech into mainstream non-tech professions like sales, HR, law, and education, signaling a shift where workers must know how to use AI tools rather than build them.

items.title: New grads have to compete with AI for entry
items.summary: A report by ResumeTemplates.com highlights a tightening job market for recent graduates across all majors, finding that 48% of hiring managers would rather invest in AI tools than hire and train an entry-level worker, placing greater emphasis on candidates' immediate AI competency and soft skills.

items.title: 10 Most Employable College Degrees In The Age Of AI
items.summary: An analysis of over 100 occupations across 24 fields identified the most AI-resilient degree fields, finding that majors involving physical interaction, heavy human judgment, or ethical oversight—such as healthcare, engineering, and business management—offer the greatest career stability.

items.title: Gallup-Lumina 2026 State of Higher Education Study: How AI is Reshaping Academic Paths
items.summary: A joint Gallup-Lumina study found that 42% of bachelor's degree students have seriously considered changing their major due to AI's disruptive potential, prompting many to pivot toward "AI-resistant" or hands-on fields such as healthcare, trades, and interdisciplinary data sciences.

items.title: 2026 AI, Automation, and the Future of Humanities Degree Careers
items.summary: This report outlines how AI is changing humanities-based careers by automating repetitive tasks, pushing graduates to acquire digital literacy, data interpretation, and AI certifications to command higher pay in roles focused on ethical storytelling and human-AI interaction.

items.title: Report Highlights Changing Views on Skilled Trades
items.summary: Drawing from Jobber's new report on Gen Z and parents of Gen Alpha, the study reveals that 68% of parents say AI has made them rethink the long-term stability of white-collar careers, driving a substantial shift toward high-paying, automation-resistant skilled trades.

items.title: Meta Selects Houston for New Skilled Trades Workforce Training Program
items.summary: Meta is launching America's Workforce Academy, a $115 million free training initiative in partnership with the National Urban League to train and guarantee jobs for electricians, welders, and fiber technicians who are critically needed to construct the physical infrastructure powering the AI boom.

items.title: Skilled Trades Survey 2026: How Gen Z Views AI & College
items.summary: A survey of Gen Z adults found that 52% of current college students believe the skilled trades (like HVAC, electrical, and plumbing) feel safer from AI-driven job disruption than traditional office-based, white-collar professions.

items.title: AI Shifts Labor Demand: Skilled Trades Gain as White-Collar Hiring Slows
items.summary: As automation increasingly handles routine cognitive desk work, major companies like Ford and AT&T are ramping up blue-collar recruitment for physical, hands-on roles like technicians, mechanics, and electricians that AI cannot replicate.
